# Kit weight — full carry weight for travel

**Dimension:** total body + lens weight for realistic travel kits, since
"lightweight" is the user's top priority. Weights are spec figures (body =
CIPA, with battery + card); real carry weight is higher once you add a strap,
filter, and spare battery. Sources in [citations.md](../citations.md).

## Body + one-lens travel kits

| Kit | Body (g) | Lens (g) | Total (g) | Notes |
|-----|----------|----------|-----------|-------|
| **(a) Lightest APS-C** | R50 375 [[1]](../citations.md#c1) | RF-S 18-150mm ~305 [[46]](../citations.md#c46) | **~680** | 28.8–240 mm-equiv all-in-one |
| **(b) Light full-frame** | R8 461 [[2]](../citations.md#c2) | RF 24-105mm f/4-7.1 395 [[43]](../citations.md#c43) | **~856** | Full-frame image quality, still light |
| **(c) Quality full-frame** | R6 II 680 [[3]](../citations.md#c3) | RF 24-105mm f/4L 700 [[42]](../citations.md#c42) | **~1,380** | IBIS, sealed, sharp — ~2× kit (a) |
| **(d) Cheapest APS-C** | R100 356 [[6]](../citations.md#c6) | RF-S 18-45mm 130 [[47]](../citations.md#c47) | **~486** | Lightest + cheapest; limited reach |

Math is additive (e.g. 375 + 305 = 680 g). All figures carry ≥2 significant
digits from the cited specs. Note: source [[46]](../citations.md#c46) reports the
RF-S 18-150mm as ~305–310 g; 305 g (the lower bound) is used here, so kit (a)
could be ~685 g at the upper bound.

## What the numbers show

- The **body is not the main weight driver — the lens is.** The full-frame R8 is
  only 86 g heavier than the APS-C R50, so a full-frame travel kit can be
  competitive once lens weight dominates
  [[1]](../citations.md#c1)[[2]](../citations.md#c2)[[63]](../citations.md#c63).
- The lightest *capable* travel kit is **(a)** at ~680 g (one lens, huge range).
- Going to top image quality **(c)** roughly doubles the carry weight.

## Counter-perspectives (weight realism)

- **Lenses dominate; body choice matters less than people think** once equivalent
  glass is attached [[64]](../citations.md#c64).
- **APS-C "equivalent" lenses can be heavier than full-frame ones** — chasing
  equivalent coverage/aperture on APS-C can erase the system weight advantage
  [[63]](../citations.md#c63). With Canon's thin RF-S line, APS-C users often
  mount heavier full-frame RF glass anyway (see
  [third-party-lenses](third-party-lenses.md)).
- **Multi-lens kits erase body savings:** carry 2–3 lenses and a ~100 g body gap
  disappears into the bag total — total kit weight, not body weight, decides
  travel comfort [[64]](../citations.md#c64)[[65]](../citations.md#c65)[[66]](../citations.md#c66).

## Practical takeaway

If lightweight + one-lens simplicity is the goal, **kit (a)** wins. If
full-frame quality matters, **kit (b)** stays light by pairing the light R8 with
the light f/4-7.1 zoom — avoid the heavy f/4L unless image quality outranks
weight.

## Gaps and limitations

- Totals are spec weights only; add ~100–300 g for strap, filter, spare battery,
  and any second lens. No reviewer-published "fully loaded bag" gram figure was
  found for these exact combos [[66]](../citations.md#c66).
- A lighter full-frame combo exists (R8 + RF 24-50mm f/4.5-6.3, ~210 g lens ≈
  671 g total) but that lens was not separately verified in-session — excluded
  from the table, noted here as a candidate.
